title: Integrated Finance & Legal Playbook: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition (2025)
author: Aisha Kapoor
summary: Company-wide playbook that defines the end-to-end processes, roles, and controls for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, procurement and purchasing, contract lifecycle management, and revenue recognition/billing policies for Redwood Inference.
body:
Overview
This playbook consolidates finance and legal procedures that govern how Redwood plans and authorizes spend, enters into commercial agreements, procures goods and services, and recognizes revenue. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, product, engineering leadership, and business owners. Follow the sections below for process steps, approval matrices, templates, and escalation points.

Scope
- Budgeting & Forecasting: Annual budgeting, quarterly reforecasts, and rolling 12-month forecasts covering OPEX, headcount, and CAPEX.
- Procurement: Purchase requisition, purchase order (PO) issuance, vendor onboarding, and purchase approvals.
- Contracts: Contract intake, redline/negotiation, legal review, signature, and storage.
- Revenue Recognition & Billing: Billing cadence, invoicing, SaaS revenue recognition rules, deferred revenue treatment, and adjustments/credits.

1) Roles and Ownership
- Finance (owner): Oversees budgeting, forecasting, revenue recognition policy, invoicing, and financial controls.
- Legal (owner): Reviews and approves contract terms, manages risk approvals, and maintains contract repository.
- Procurement / FinanceOps: Manages vendor onboarding, PO issuance, procurement tooling, and supplier payments.
- Business Owner (requesting team): Owns requirements, budget request, vendor selection, and validation of deliverables.
- Finance Approver Matrix: Manager -> Director -> VP Finance -> CFO (based on thresholds below).

2) Budgeting & Forecasting Process
- Annual Budget Cycle (timeline):
  1. Budget kickoff (Nov): Finance publishes templates and target guidance (revenue, growth, headcount bands).
  2. Department submissions (Dec): Teams submit base budgets with narrative and variance drivers.
  3. Finance reviews & iterations (Dec–Jan): Finance meets with each owner for 1:1s to reconcile assumptions.
  4. Executive review & approval (Jan–Feb): Finance presents consolidated budget for leadership approval.
  5. Board submission (Feb): Final approved budget is delivered to the Board.
- Rolling Forecasts: Monthly rolling 12-month forecast updated by the 7th business day. Forecast must include: revenue, gross margin, headcount plan, committed spend (contracts/POs), and runway.
- Budgeting Templates: Use the Finance Budget Template (Drive link) with line-item categories: Personnel, Cloud/GPU, Third‑party SaaS, Professional Services, Marketing, Travel, Capital Projects.
- Variance Control: Any variance >10% or $50k for a line item requires re-approval by the original approver level.

3) Procurement and Purchase Approvals
- Thresholds & Approvals:
  - <$10,000: Manager approval + FinanceOps notification.
  - $10,000–$100,000: Director approval + FinanceOps review.
  - $100,000–$500,000: VP approval + Legal quick review (commercial terms checklist).
  - >$500,000: CFO approval + Legal SLA and risk committee sign-off.
- Procurement Flow (standard purchase):
  1. Requestor completes Purchase Requisition (PR) in ProcureFlow tool with business justification and budget code.
  2. FinanceOps validates budget availability and creates a PO if approved.
  3. Vendor receives PO; services or goods delivered per SOW.
  4. Invoices routed to AP with PO number; three‑way match required (PO, invoice, receipt/acceptance).
- Sole-Source / Strategic Vendor Exceptions: For sole-source purchases or strategic vendor relationships (including cloud GPU capacity and model licensing), the requestor must provide a competitive-intelligence memo and obtain Director-level approval plus Legal pre-review.
- Approved Vendor Onboarding: Vendors must complete KYC, security questionnaire (for data access vendors), and payment terms questionnaire. FinanceOps owns vendor master data in our ERP.

4) Contract Lifecycle (high level)
- Intake & Standardization:
  - Use the Contract Intake Form (linked) to capture scope, term, commercial terms, and data handling requirements. Business owner completes intake and selects template: Master Services Agreement (MSA), Statement of Work (SOW), Data Processing Addendum (DPA), or Reseller Agreement.
- Review & Negotiation:
  1. Legal reviews contract against standard playbook (SLA, IP, liability, indemnity, data residency).
  2. Redline exchange: Use collaborative redlines in the Legal workspace; aim for first turnaround within 5 business days for standard MSAs and 10 business days for complex agreements.
  3. Escalation: Any non-standard liability cap, indemnity, or change to data residency requires Legal + VP product or VP infra sign-off.
- Signature & Storage:
  - Approved signers: Legal may designate signatory limits. Standard MSAs under $250k may be signed by VP-level; >$250k require CFO/CEO as per delegation matrix.
  - Execution: Prefer e-signature (DocuSign). After signature, Legal uploads executed documents to the Contract Repository (contracts.redwood.internal). FinanceOps tags contracts that create revenue commitments for RevRec tracking.

5) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies
- Revenue Types & Policy Summary:
  - Hosted API usage (usage-based): Recognize revenue as usage occurs (measured monthly). For prepaid credits, recognize as deferred revenue and amortize as consumed.
  - Dedicated capacity (reserved contracts): Recognize revenue ratably over the service period unless performance obligations indicate otherwise. Upfront implementation fees: allocate between setup (recognized on completion of setup milestone) and ongoing service (ratable).
  - Private deployment (license + support): Distinguish between license (might require different treatment) and recurring support. License revenue recognition follows ASC 606 principles: identify performance obligations and determine transaction price allocation.
- Billing Cadence & Invoicing:
  - Standard customers: Monthly invoicing in arrears for usage and recurring fees.
  - Enterprise customers: Net-30 default; exceptions require FinanceOps approval and credit assessment.
  - Prepaid/Committed credits: Invoice on contract signature; record as deferred revenue and release on usage.
- Deferred Revenue & Contract Liabilities:
  - Finance records deferred revenue for any amounts invoiced but not yet earned. Monthly close processes must reconcile deferred revenue ledger to active contracts.
- Credits, Adjustments & Disputes:
  - Credits for SLA breaches: Calculate per SLA terms; issue credit memo in the billing system and reduce future invoices or issue refunds subject to Finance approval.
  - Billing disputes: Customer must submit disputes within 60 days. FinanceOps investigates; if validated, issue adjustment within 30 days of validation.

6) Controls, Auditability & Reporting
- Segregation of Duties: Requestors cannot approve their own POs; Legal negotiators should not approve payment requests.
- Audit Trail: All POs, contracts, and invoices must be stored with traceable change logs. ProcureFlow and Contract Repository retain version history for at least 7 years.
- Monthly Close: Finance runs month-end close checklist including revenue cutoffs, deferred revenue reconciliations, and contract liability reviews.
- KPIs & Dashboards: Finance publishes: burn rate, runway (months), backlog (annual recurring revenue committed but not billed), DSO, and contract renewal schedule.

7) Templates and Checklists (appendix)
- Attachments (links to internal Drive/Repos):
  - Finance Budget Template (XLSX)
  - Purchase Requisition Form (ProcureFlow)
  - Contract Intake Form (Confluence link)
  - Standard MSA and SOW templates (Legal repo)
  - Revenue recognition checklist for new product offers
- Purchase Requisition checklist (minimum required fields):
  1. Business justification and budget code
  2. Vendor legal name and remit-to address
  3. Contract/SOW reference (if applicable)
  4. Estimated total cost, including tax and freight
  5. Expected delivery date and acceptance criteria

8) Escalation Paths and Contacts
- Procurement exceptions and urgent hardware requests: FinanceOps (finops@redwood.internal) -> Director, FinanceOps (Miguel Alvarez).
- Contract risk beyond standard terms: Legal (legal@redwood.internal) -> Head of Legal (Priya Raman).
- Revenue recognition edge cases: Finance (revrec@redwood.internal) -> VP Finance (Daniel Cho).

9) Change Management & Continuous Improvement
- Policy Review Cadence: This playbook is reviewed annually in Q4 and after any material change to accounting standards or procurement tooling.
- Feedback Loop: Business owners should send process improvement suggestions to finops-feedback@redwood.internal. Finance tracks and publishes change tickets and implementation timelines.

Appendix: Common Scenarios (quick guidance)
- Cloud GPU reserved capacity purchase (>$100k): Follow procurement flow, engage Legal early for SLAs, and route to VP approval.
- Customer committed usage with tiered discounts: Document thresholds in SOW; recognize revenue ratably and monitor uplift/true‑up each quarter.
- Prepaid credits for hosted API: Invoice on signature, record deferred revenue, and amortize on consumption.

Contact and Ownership
